chapter: Reel 2: Los Angeles musicians, the Apex and Cotton Club
title: Jake Porter, hard to get along with
summary: Howard says he avoided Jake Porter because he was difficult and fussy.

story.theme_name: Leading a band: choosing, paying and managing players

blocks.x: Now, is there somebody you enjoyed playing with, the trumpet player, Jake Porter?
No, I didn't care about Jake. I'm going to tell you the truth. I'm going to tell you the truth. I --
Jake and I didn't -- well, he was a little difficult to get along with. And I just would stay away from people that was hard to get along with.
That's okay, I understand that. What about Teddy Buckner?
(Inaudible). He'll be mad at me forever.
Okay. (Unintelligible.) She promised that you will give the okay and we can always cut. We can always cut. No, he won't get into this.
This will be kept in the Smithsonian and nobody will -- outside the Smithsonian will ever hear this unless you say. It's all up to you, Mr. Howard.
He'll be back here to want to kill me.
No, go ahead, because -- no, you can
okay anything and the main thing is to get some of the facts down here.
The facts about -- you know who it was, Buddy? Jake was hard to get along with. And you know, he's fussy and squabbly.
When he's on the board at the union, I can see that.
Yeah, he fuss all the time.
